articles.title: When to Visit Northern Portugal: A Season for Every Kind of Stay
articles.content:
A spring walk above the coast, a long summer lunch after the beach, a vineyard visit in September or a winter weekend with a chef cooking at home: northern Portugal offers several different holidays within the same region. Start with the experience you want to bring home, then choose your dates.

For a first visit combining towns, nature and time outside, our suggested shortlist is May, June and September. For school-holiday beach days, compare July and August. For a shorter escape centred on food, culture and a beautiful house, there is much to enjoy throughout the year.

## Choose your season by the holiday you want

| Your ideal stay | Dates to compare | What to prioritise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coast, towns and a little adventure | May, June or September | A well-placed base and one or two guided experiences. |
| Family beach holiday | July and August, or your school-holiday dates | The right bedrooms, outdoor space and convenient beach access. |
| Vineyards and regional food | September and October, or a tasting at another time | A confirmed winery visit; harvest participation is a separate arrangement. |
| A weekend for two | Any month | Privacy, a comfortable home and a dinner or experience you can enjoy together. |
| Walking and cycling | Spring and autumn dates | A route matched to your group and the local conditions. |

These are itinerary suggestions, not promises about a particular week. Coastal Minho, the Douro and higher ground in the northern interior have different settings. The [IPMA climate reference](https://www.ipma.pt/pt/oclima/normais.clima/) helps explain those differences; use the local forecast closer to departure to fine-tune your plans.

## Spring: green landscapes and days made for exploring

### March and April

Make your base part of the pleasure: breakfast together, a town to explore, a walk and a generous lunch. Viana do Castelo works well for a short stay combining its historic centre with Santa Luzia and the waterfront. Easter dates vary each year, so check opening arrangements for any visit around which you are building the trip.

### May and June

For a first northern holiday, these months deserve a place on your shortlist. Plan an [e-bike outing](/experiences/ebike-tours), a [horseback ride](/experiences/horseback-riding) or a day discovering the coast, then keep an afternoon for the house. Families with children outside school age can build a slower itinerary without organising every hour.

![Horse riders following a coastal path in Viana do Castelo](/experiences/horseback-riding/03.webp)
A moment from the Portugal Active riding catalogue. [Explore the experience](/experiences/horseback-riding).

## Summer: beach mornings and evenings together

### July and August

Choose a home that supports the way your group spends the day. Some people want to surf before lunch; others want a garden, a book and a place in the shade. A base near Viana, Caminha or Esposende can combine those preferences, provided the actual journeys work for everyone.

For a beach-led stay, [compare northern beaches and bases](/blog/complete-guide-north-portugal). Sea views and walking access to the sand are different benefits: check both on the property page. Ask about cooling, outdoor dining and pool arrangements where they matter to your group. Lifeguard supervision is seasonal and beach-specific; follow the flags and local instructions when swimming.

If the trip centres on a festival, use the organiser's dates for the year you are travelling. Choose essential bookings together: a large home, the preferred experience and any transfer needed to connect them. That is more useful than relying on a last-minute match for several families.

## Autumn: wine, food and a more leisurely itinerary

### September and October

Picture a morning outside, a winery visit and a long meal with no need to rush back to another appointment. September and October make a natural theme for a food-and-wine stay, whether you choose the Minho or spend part of the trip in the Douro.

Book a tasting for its own merits. Harvest activities depend on the producer, grapes and actual picking dates; a visit in September does not automatically include grape picking. If the Douro is the focus, [stay in the valley](/destinations/douro) rather than designing every day around a return journey from the coast.

For a Minho base, combine a local outing with a [private chef dinner](/services/private-chef). It gives the group a shared evening at home and leaves the daytime programme open to different interests.

## Winter: a beautiful home and a reason to slow down

### November to February

Think of a short winter stay as its own kind of holiday. Choose a comfortable living room, a dining table you will use and bedrooms suited to the group. Add a cultural visit, a favourite restaurant or an evening prepared by a chef. In [Viana](/blog/viana-do-castelo-guide), the Museu do Traje and Gil Eannes tell different parts of the city's story; in [Porto](/destinations/porto), make time for art, architecture and the riverfront.

Heating, access and the location of the home matter more than an attractive photograph alone. A pool described as heated needs its own details checked: operating dates, any extra charge and the arrangement for your stay. Christmas and New Year also deserve specific meal and arrival plans, with opening days confirmed directly.

![A Portugal Active chef serving dinner to a couple](/experiences/private-chef-dinner.webp)
An evening at home can be a highlight of the trip. [Plan a private chef dinner](/blog/private-chef-portugal-villa).

## Turn a preferred month into a real stay

Choose the base first: [Minho, northern Portugal](/destinations/minho), [Porto](/destinations/porto) or [Douro](/destinations/douro). Then compare actual dates, guest numbers and the same booking conditions. A month alone does not tell you the total cost or which homes are available.

If you have a week, our [family itinerary for northern Portugal](/blog/northern-portugal-family-holiday-itinerary) shows how to leave space for the house as well as the region. For a weekend, one destination and one memorable experience are often enough.

Send the team your preferred dates, an alternative if you have one, and the two things that matter most: perhaps the beach and a pool, or privacy and good food. [Plan your stay with Portugal Active](/contact?subject=plan-my-stay&destination=minho).

articles.title: Surfing in Northern Portugal: Plan a Minho Coast Stay
articles.content:
The best part of a surf holiday in northern Portugal can be its rhythm: a morning in the water, lunch by the coast and an afternoon with no need to go far. On the Minho coast, you can build that holiday around Viana do Castelo and still make room for towns, countryside and evenings at your own holiday home.

This guide is for choosing the shape of the trip. The [surf lesson page](/experiences/surf-lessons) is where to check the current experience and request a session. Your instructor chooses the beach and session around the group and the conditions; a place name alone cannot make that decision.

## Choose a base before choosing a surf spot

| Base | A good fit for | What to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Viana do Castelo and Cabedelo | A trip combining lessons, the city and the coast. | The journey from the home to the agreed meeting point. |
| Afife and the coast north of Viana | A stay with the coastal landscape at its centre. | Car or transfer arrangements and where lessons actually meet. |
| Moledo and Caminha | A beach holiday with time in Caminha and the Minho estuary. | Whether the selected lesson operates near your base. |
| Esposende and Ofir | Beach time combined with the Cávado riverfront and nearby walks. | Lesson availability and the particular home’s beach access. |

[Turismo de Portugal's northern beach guide](https://www.visitportugal.com/en/destinos/porto-e-norte/412643) highlights Afife and Cabedelo for surfing and describes the coast around Moledo, Viana and Esposende. Use that geography to shortlist a base, then let a local instructor advise on the session itself. Avoid choosing accommodation around an assumed tide, wave height or daily lesson location.

## Your first surf lesson: what matters most

Tell the team whether you have never surfed, have tried a few times or can already catch waves independently. Being comfortable swimming is different from having surf experience; both are useful information. Share the ages of children and ask which session is appropriate for the whole group.

A first session should leave time for an introduction, equipment fitting and practice with the instructor. Ask what is included, where to meet, the total duration and how much of that time is spent in the water. If you want more individual attention, ask about a private lesson; if friends are learning together, compare a group session.

- Confirm the board, wetsuit and other equipment supplied for your size and level.
- Bring swimwear, a towel, sun protection and dry clothes for afterwards.
- Arrange the journey to the meeting point and back before setting out.
- Tell the organiser about anything that could affect participation when booking.

The current catalogue's age and participation requirements apply to the experience. Check those details with the team when travelling with children; a general guide cannot confirm eligibility for an individual child.

## One lesson or several days?

For a first taste, reserve one session early enough in the stay to leave room for another if you enjoy it. For a trip centred on learning, discuss a series of lessons and the progression you want before booking several unrelated sessions. The aim is time to practise, not simply a busy calendar.

Experienced surfers should explain the kind of waves and guidance they are seeking. A beginner lesson and an exploration of local breaks are different requests. Confirm whether the proposed service includes guiding, equipment or transport rather than assuming all three are part of the price.

![Riders on the coast during a Portugal Active horseback outing](/experiences/horseback-riding/03.webp)
There is plenty to enjoy between sessions. [Discover horseback riding in Viana](/experiences/horseback-riding).

## Build a three-day surf break

**Day one:** arrive, settle into the home and enjoy a walk or meal near your base. Keep the first evening easy, especially after a flight.

**Day two:** make the surf session the main plan. Leave time afterwards for lunch, a rest and the house. If the group has different interests, the [Viana city guide](/blog/viana-do-castelo-guide) gives non-surfers a rewarding day of their own.

**Day three:** choose a second session or another way to explore. An [e-bike tour](/experiences/ebike-tours) brings a different view of the coast. A [private chef dinner](/services/private-chef) can bring everyone back together without another journey at the end of the day.

This is a suggested rhythm, not a package or a fixed timetable. With a longer stay, add unplanned time between the active days.

## Choose a home that works after the beach

Start with the [beach villa collection](/collections/beach-villas) or [homes in the Minho](/homes?destination=minho). Compare the layout for your group, the route to the lesson, places to relax and outdoor dining. If bringing boards, ask about storage and transport; do not assume every property has specialist facilities.

A sea view does not automatically mean walking access to the sand. Likewise, a home in the municipality of Viana may be outside the centre. Check the particular address and travel arrangements, especially if some of the group will not have a car.

## Arrive with the practical details already organised

Porto Airport is a useful starting point for a Minho trip. If you are staying in central Viana, compare the [direct GET BUS airport connection](https://www.getbus.eu/pt/viana-do-castelo-aeroporto) with a private transfer. A shuttle to the house can be arranged through our team; include surfboard bags, luggage and children's seat requirements in the request. A city bus arrival still leaves the final journey to the accommodation.

[Explore the surf experience](/experiences/surf-lessons), then share your dates, base, group and level. We can help connect the session with the rest of your stay.

articles.title: A Wine Lover's Guide to the Douro Valley and Vinho Verde Region
articles.content:
Northern Portugal has two wine regions that could not be more different. The Douro Valley produces powerful reds and the world's most famous fortified wine from terraced vineyards carved into schist mountains. The Vinho Verde region, just to the west, produces fresh, aromatic whites from granite pergola vines in one of Europe's greenest landscapes.

Together, they make northern Portugal one of the most rewarding wine destinations in the world. More intimate than Bordeaux, less touristed than Tuscany, and with a diversity that means you can taste two radically different wine cultures in a single day.

### The Douro Valley: power, history, and terraces

The Douro Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the landscape alone justifies the designation. Steep mountainsides covered in hand-built stone terraces, the Douro River winding through the valley floor, and a silence that feels almost physical.

Wine has been made here for over two thousand years. The Romans planted vines. The Portuguese refined them. And in the 18th century, the British discovered that adding grape spirit to the wine preserved it for the long sea journey to England. Port wine was born.

Today, the Douro produces three things that matter to wine lovers:

**Port wine** remains the headline act. Vintage Ports, Late Bottled Vintages, Tawnies aged 10, 20, 30, 40 years. The quintas along the Douro hold some of the most extraordinary wines in the world, many of which are only available at the estate.

**Douro reds** have emerged in the last twenty years as some of Portugal's finest table wines. Made from indigenous grapes (Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz), they combine power with elegance. The best rival anything from the Rhone or Piedmont.

**Douro whites** are the sleeper. White wines from Viosinho, Rabigato, and Gouveio grapes, grown on high-altitude schist soils, produce wines of intensity and minerality that surprise even seasoned wine professionals.

**Quintas to visit:**

**Quinta do Crasto.** One of the Douro's most respected estates. Stunning terrace overlooking the river. The Reserva wines are exceptional. Private tastings can be arranged.

**Quinta da Pacheca.** Beautiful grounds, a wine hotel, and one of the more accessible visits in the valley. Good introduction for visitors new to the Douro.

**Quinta do Vallado.** A historic estate with a modern winery designed by architect Alvaro Siza Vieira. The wines match the architecture: precise, contemporary, and bold.

**Niepoort.** Not a traditional quinta but one of the most innovative producers in the region. Dirk Niepoort has challenged every convention in Portuguese winemaking. The Charme red is a benchmark.

### Vinho Verde: the wine most people underestimate

Outside Portugal, Vinho Verde has a reputation as cheap, fizzy, and forgettable. This reputation is based on the mass market bottles sold in supermarkets for a few euros, and it does those wines an injustice. At the premium end, Vinho Verde is one of Europe's most exciting white wine regions.

The key grape is **Alvarinho**, grown principally in the sub-regions of Moncao and Melgaco near the Spanish border. These wines are aromatic, textured, and capable of aging. They bear no resemblance to the supermarket Vinho Verde most people have encountered.

Other grapes worth knowing: **Loureiro** (floral, aromatic), **Avesso** (rich, structured), and **Trajadura** (fruity, approachable). The best producers blend them with intelligence and skill.

**Producers to visit:**

**Quinta de Soalheiro (Melgaco).** The family that essentially defined modern Alvarinho. Multiple ranges from accessible to collectible. Private tastings in a beautiful setting. The drive through the Minho valley to reach them is part of the experience.

**Anselmo Mendes (Moncao).** Perhaps the most respected winemaker in the Vinho Verde region. His single-vineyard Alvarinhos (Muros Antigos, Contacto) demonstrate what this grape can really do.

**Quinta da Lixa.** A larger producer making consistently excellent wines at every price point. The Pouco Comum Alvarinho is remarkable value.

**Quinta de Santiago (Celorico de Basto).** A newer producer in the eastern Vinho Verde area, working with both white and red varieties. Intimate tastings and a beautiful estate.

### The difference between visiting alone and visiting with a concierge

You can absolutely drive the Douro or the Vinho Verde route yourself. The roads are good, the scenery is extraordinary, and many quintas accept walk-in visitors. But there is a significant difference between showing up at the tourist tasting bar and receiving a private tour with the winemaker.

When our [concierge arranges a wine experience](/experiences#gastronomy), what changes is access. The producers we work with open doors that are closed to casual visitors. You taste barrel samples. You meet the family. You sit in the vineyard instead of a tasting room. And you do not drive, because a private driver means you can taste without restraint.

A typical day arranged by our concierge:

Morning departure from your property. Drive to the first producer for a private tasting (typically 1 to 1.5 hours, including vineyard walk). Lunch at a restaurant the producer recommends (or at the quinta if they offer it). Second tasting in the afternoon at a different style of producer. Return to your property by late afternoon, carrying the wines you purchased. Total: 5 to 7 hours.

For deeper immersion: multi-day wine itineraries covering both the Douro and Vinho Verde regions, with overnight stays at wine estates and meals at estate restaurants.

### Harvest season: the ultimate wine experience

If you can time your visit for late September through mid-October, the harvest transforms both regions. Vineyards are active with pickers. The air smells of grape must. Some producers allow guests to participate in the harvest (picking, treading, blending).

This is wine country at its most alive. The restaurants serve harvest menus. The new wines begin fermenting. And the autumn light in the Douro Valley, golden and warm against the red and orange vine leaves, is genuinely one of the most beautiful sights in Europe.

### Where to stay for a wine trip

The Douro Valley itself has limited high-quality accommodation. Several quintas offer rooms, but availability is limited, particularly during harvest.

Our recommendation: base yourself at one of our properties in the Minho or Porto area and visit the wine regions on day trips arranged by concierge.

**For Vinho Verde access:** Any of our [Minho Coast properties](/homes?region=minho-coast) puts you within an hour of the best producers. [Lima River Houses](/homes/lima-river-houses-by-portugal-active-7431cb) in Ponte de Lima is positioned at the heart of the Vinho Verde region.

**For Douro access:** Our [Porto properties](/homes?region=porto-douro) are 90 minutes from the central Douro Valley. Combine city exploration with wine country.

**For both:** Stay a week, split between regions. Our concierge plans the logistics.

articles.title: A Private Chef at Your Portugal Villa: Menus, Costs and Planning
articles.content:
After a day on the coast, everyone comes back to the same table. A private chef meal can turn the house into the setting for an evening together: no separate restaurant journey, space for conversation and a menu discussed around your group.

The best starting point is the meal you want to share. A birthday dinner, a family lunch and an evening for two need different planning. Use this guide to prepare the request, then explore our [private chef service in Portugal](/services/private-chef) for the current starting price and an individual proposal.

## Choose the occasion and the pace

**For a couple:** describe whether you want a relaxed dinner or a more formal sequence of courses. Share any favourite dishes and whether you would like a drinks proposal.

**For families:** give the number and ages of children, preferred meal time and any simpler dishes to discuss. Agree whether everyone eats together or whether the proposal should include a different serving order.

**For a group:** explain the bedroom and dining arrangements at the house, how many people will sit down and whether you prefer sharing dishes or individual plates. For larger groups, kitchen capacity, seating and service arrangements matter as much as the menu.

**For an occasion:** describe the celebration when enquiring. Additional visitors, music, decoration and late finishes must fit the home's rules. A chef booking does not by itself authorise an event.

![A Portugal Active chef serving dinner at home](/experiences/private-chef-dinner.webp)
An evening from the Portugal Active catalogue. Menu and service are agreed for each booking.

## What affects the cost of a private chef?

The published service has a starting price, while the confirmed quote depends on the date, location, group size, menu and service requested. Compare the total for the group as well as any per-person figure. Ask how children, minimum charges, travel and optional extras are handled.

| Part of the proposal | Ask for this detail |
| --- | --- |
| Food | The agreed dishes, ingredients and alternatives |
| Drinks | Whether drinks, pairing or corkage are included or separate |
| Service | Chef time, any service staff and the planned meal time |
| House preparation | Kitchen equipment, tableware, seating and any hire needs |
| Finishing the evening | Kitchen cleaning, waste and the service end time |
| Booking | Total price, payment schedule and cancellation conditions |

These are points to confirm, not a list of automatic inclusions. A clear written proposal lets you compare the experience you are actually buying.

## Menus, preferences and dietary requirements

Think in terms of a meal you would enjoy: Portuguese flavours, Mediterranean dishes or another preference to discuss with the team. Seasonal ingredients can guide the conversation, but an example menu is only agreed once it is confirmed for your date.

Send allergies and dietary requirements with the first request. Ask the chef to confirm whether they can accommodate them, including any relevant preparation requirements. Do not assume that a menu description establishes suitability for every guest.

## Preparing the villa

Share the home's name or booking reference and whether you imagine eating inside or outside. Confirm access for the chef, kitchen equipment and a table large enough for the group. If the property belongs to a partner or another host, confirm that the service is permitted there.

If you are still choosing a home, browse [homes for larger groups](/collections/large-group-villas) or [homes with pools](/collections/villas-with-private-pool). Choose the house for the stay as a whole; chef availability and the suitability of the kitchen are checked separately.

![A table being prepared for a meal at home](/experiences/private-chef-table.webp)
Make the setting part of the evening. Table arrangements and service are agreed in your proposal.

## Requesting your meal

- Your preferred date, meal time and location or home.
- Number of adults and children, with children's ages.
- The occasion, preferred style and approximate budget.
- Allergies, dietary requirements and drinks preferences.
- Any extra visitors, equipment or arrangements to discuss.

With those details, the team can check availability and prepare a proposal. A request is not a confirmed booking; the final menu, total and conditions should be agreed before you commit.

[Request a private chef for your stay](/contact?subject=services-enquiry&service=private-chef), or [see the service page](/services/private-chef) to start planning an evening at home.

articles.title: Behind the Scenes: How We Prepare Every Home to Hotel Standards
articles.content:
The phrase "hotel standards" is easy to claim. Every property management company uses it. Few can explain what it actually means when applied to a private home where there is no lobby, no housekeeping team of fifty, and no brand manual thick enough to stop a door.

We can explain it. Because we wrote the manual.

### What hotel standards actually means

In a hotel, consistency is structural. The building was designed for service. The corridors exist for housekeeping carts. The linens are laundered in a basement facility. The amenities arrive in bulk from a supplier who serves a thousand rooms.

In a private home, none of this infrastructure exists. Each property is different: different layouts, different owners, different kitchens, different standards of what "clean" means to the person who lived there last.

Our job is to make every one of these individual homes feel like the same calibre of experience. Not identical. Each home has its own personality, and that is part of the charm. But the baseline, the things a guest should never have to think about, must be consistent across every property.

That baseline is what we call the operating standard.

### Before every arrival

Our team visits every property before every guest arrival. Not a quick check. A systematic walkthrough using a checklist that covers over 40 points.

**Linens and bedding.** Every bed is made with hotel-grade white linens (300+ thread count cotton). Duvets, pillows, and mattress protectors are inspected and replaced on schedule. Extra pillows and blankets are placed in each bedroom. Towels are full-size bath sheets, not the thin towels that are the hallmark of amateur rentals.

**Bathroom.** Full-size amenities (shampoo, conditioner, body wash, hand soap) from a curated brand. Not travel sachets. Fresh hand towels and bath towels. Clean, dry, and staged. Toilet paper stocked (a detail that sounds trivial until you arrive at midnight to find the previous guest used the last roll).

**Kitchen.** Every appliance tested and working. Coffee machine cleaned and loaded. Basic provisions checked (coffee, tea, sugar, olive oil, salt, pepper, cleaning supplies). Dishwasher emptied. Surfaces clean. Bins empty and lined. Ice in the freezer.

**Living areas.** Cushions arranged. Throws folded. Entertainment systems tested (wifi confirmed working, TV operational, streaming services signed in where applicable). Lighting checked (every bulb working, every switch functional). Temperature set appropriately for the season.

**Outdoor areas.** Pool cleaned and tested (water chemistry verified that morning). Garden tidy. Terrace furniture clean and positioned. Barbecue clean and functional. Outdoor lighting working.

**Safety.** Smoke detectors tested. First aid kit stocked. Emergency numbers posted. Property access instructions verified.

**Welcome.** Welcome hamper placed (local wine, water, fruit, and a selection of regional products). Welcome note with key information (wifi password, appliance instructions, local emergency numbers, concierge contact).

This entire process takes our team two to four hours per property. It happens before every single arrival. Every time.

### The invisible work

Most of what our team does, guests never see. And that is exactly the point.

**Maintenance.** Our operations team monitors every property continuously. The dripping tap gets fixed before the guest notices. The pool pump that sounds different gets serviced before it fails. The garden that grows too fast in spring gets extra cuts. Preventive maintenance is not glamorous. It is the reason things work when you expect them to.

**Vendor relationships.** We do not outsource to a different cleaning company each week. Our housekeeping team knows every property. They know where the tricky corners are in each kitchen, which shower glass streaks if you use the wrong product, and which terrace collects leaves faster than others. This consistency comes from working with the same people, trained to the same standard, across every property.

**Quality audits.** Every property undergoes a quarterly review. Beyond the daily checks, this deeper audit evaluates furniture condition, appliance lifespan, linen quality, paint and surface condition, and the overall "feel" of the property. Properties that fall below standard receive remediation plans. Properties that consistently exceed standard are promoted within our portfolio.

### What guests notice (and what they do not)

Guests notice the crisp white sheets. They notice the good coffee in the morning. They notice the pool being clean when they come down for a swim. They notice the wifi working. They notice the welcome hamper.

They do not notice that the previous guests spilled red wine on the sofa cushion and our team replaced the cover at 6am. They do not notice that the air conditioning filter was cleaned last Tuesday. They do not notice that the chef's knives in the kitchen are sharpened quarterly.

They should not notice. The absence of problems is not an experience you consciously register. But it is the reason your stay feels effortless rather than merely adequate. It is the reason you relax faster than you expected. And it is the reason many guests tell us, at the end of their stay, that everything "just worked."

That feeling is not luck. It is a checklist, a team, and a standard applied relentlessly.

### Returning guests: the standard evolves

For guests who come back (and over 60% do), the standard becomes personal.

Our concierge team records preferences. Not in a creepy, surveillance way. In the way a great hotel remembers that you prefer a firm pillow, or that you drink oat milk, or that you always ask for an early check-in because you land at 7am.

On your second visit, the welcome hamper includes the wine you loved the first time. The pillows match your preference. The fridge has oat milk.

On your third visit, we know you like to surf on your first morning, so the concierge sends the forecast the night before.

This is what we mean by "anticipation, not reaction." The standard for first-time guests is high. The standard for returning guests is personal. Both require systems. Neither happens by accident.

### Why this matters

There are thousands of beautiful homes in Portugal available for rent. Many of them have pools, views, and terraces that photograph beautifully. But a beautiful home with inconsistent service is a gamble. You might arrive to perfection. You might arrive to a broken dishwasher and no towels.

Our operating standard exists to remove the gamble. To guarantee that the home you booked is the home you experience. Every time, in every property, regardless of the season or the circumstances.

Others rent homes. We operate them.

[Explore our collection](/homes) and see what a private hotel looks like in practice.

articles.title: Why We Operate Homes Instead of Listing Them
articles.content:
There are two ways to put a private home in front of a traveller.

The first is to list it. Create a profile on a marketplace, upload photos, write a description, set a price, and wait for bookings. The owner handles check-in, or hires someone. A cleaner comes between guests. A plumber is called when something breaks. The guest experience depends on the individual owner, the individual cleaner, and the individual plumber. If all three are excellent, the stay is excellent. If any one of them falls short, the stay suffers.

This is how the vast majority of private homes are offered to travellers. It is efficient, scalable, and it works well enough for a large number of people.

The second way is to operate it. Take responsibility for everything that happens inside that home. Staff it with your own team. Set standards that apply regardless of which property a guest books. Inspect, maintain, and prepare every home to the same level. Handle every guest interaction, from first enquiry to departure, with a single team trained to a single standard.

This is what we do. And this is why.

### The marketplace problem

Marketplaces transformed travel. Airbnb, Booking.com, and their competitors gave travellers access to millions of properties worldwide. They democratised accommodation. They created extraordinary choice. For this, they deserve credit.

But marketplaces have a structural limitation: they aggregate supply, they do not control it. The platform can verify photos and collect reviews. It cannot guarantee that the sheets are clean, the wifi works, or someone will answer the phone when the hot water stops at 11pm.

This is not a criticism of the platform model. It is a description of its boundaries. And for travellers who have been burned (the property that did not match the photos, the owner who disappeared after check-in, the cleaning standard that varied wildly between visits), those boundaries are felt sharply.

The premium end of the market has tried to solve this with curation: Airbnb Luxe (now discontinued), Plum Guide, Le Collectionist. These platforms select properties more carefully and add concierge layers. But the fundamental structure remains the same: they curate and distribute. They do not operate.

### What "operated" means in practice

When we say we operate a home, we mean:

**Our team does the housekeeping.** Not a contractor. Not a different cleaner each week. Our trained team, who knows every property, follows the same checklist, and is accountable to us. [We detailed our preparation process in a separate article](/journal/hotel-standards-behind-the-scenes).

**Our team handles maintenance.** When something breaks, the guest calls us. Not the owner, not a random handyman. Our operations team, who has the access codes, knows the property's quirks, and carries spare parts for the things that break most often.

**Our team runs the concierge.** When a guest wants a [private chef](/experiences#gastronomy), a [surf lesson](/experiences#adventure), or an [airport transfer](/experiences#mobility), they contact our concierge. We arrange everything using our own vetted providers, at prices we control, with quality we guarantee.

**Our team manages check-in.** No lockboxes. No self-service key collection from a cafe. A member of our local team meets you, shows you the property, explains how everything works, and gives you their phone number for the duration of your stay.

**Our team audits quality.** Every property is reviewed quarterly against our operating standard. Properties that do not meet the standard are improved or removed from our portfolio.

This is what a hotel does. The difference is that we do it across more than seventy private homes instead of two hundred rooms in a single building.

### The guest difference

For the guest, the difference between a listed home and an operated home is felt immediately.

**Consistency.** Whether you book a two-bedroom apartment in Porto or a twelve-bedroom estate in the Minho, the service standard is the same. The linens are the same quality. The concierge response time is the same. The housekeeping standard is the same. This consistency is what allows guests to book with confidence, even when choosing a property they have never seen in a region they have never visited.

**Accountability.** If something goes wrong (and in any property, things occasionally go wrong), there is a single point of contact who owns the problem. Not an owner in another city. Not a platform support centre in another country. Our local team, on the ground, with the ability to fix things immediately.

**Service depth.** A listed property offers accommodation. An operated property offers an experience. The difference is between "here are the keys" and "here is your welcome hamper, your concierge is available on WhatsApp, your chef is confirmed for Thursday, and I noticed you mentioned your anniversary so we have left a bottle of wine you might enjoy."

### The owner difference

This model works for property owners too, and it is worth explaining why, because the quality of our relationship with owners directly affects the guest experience.

Owners who list their homes on marketplaces spend time managing bookings, coordinating cleaners, handling guest communications, and dealing with maintenance issues. Some enjoy this. Many do not.

Our model is different. The owner entrusts their property to us. We handle everything: marketing, bookings, pricing, guest communication, housekeeping, maintenance, and quality control. The owner receives regular reporting and revenue without the operational burden.

This alignment matters. When the owner is not stressed about managing their property, the property is better maintained. When the property is better maintained, the guest experience is better. When the guest experience is better, reviews improve, occupancy rises, and revenue grows. Everyone benefits.

### Why we chose this model

We could have built a marketplace. It would have been easier to scale, cheaper to operate, and faster to grow. Marketplaces are capital-efficient. They are also interchangeable.

We chose to operate because we believe that hospitality is not a listing. It is a relationship between a guest and a team. The listing is just the introduction. Everything that matters happens after the booking.

The trade-off is that we grow more slowly. We can only add properties as fast as we can train teams and maintain standards. We will never have ten thousand properties. We will have five hundred properties, each operated to a level that makes guests return.

This is not the right model for everyone. Travellers who want the cheapest option, or the most options, or the maximum flexibility of an entire continent of listings, should use a marketplace. They exist for a reason and they are good at what they do.

But for travellers who want to know, before they arrive, that the home will be prepared, the team will be present, and the experience will be consistent, the operated model exists. And that is what we are building.

### See for yourself

[Browse our collection of homes](/homes). Every home we manage is one we operate, staff, and stand behind.

[Talk to our concierge](/contact) if you want to understand what this looks like in practice. Or read what our guests say about the difference.

articles.title: Viana do Castelo: One of the Most Welcoming Cities in the World
articles.content:
Booking.com analysed over 309 million reviews to determine the most welcoming cities on Earth — and Viana do Castelo ranked third in the world. For those of us who call this place home, the recognition came as no surprise.

Viana do Castelo is a city where history and nature converge in ways that few places can match. The Basilica de Santa Luzia crowns the hilltop with panoramic views that stretch across the Lima River estuary to the open Atlantic. Below, the city centre is a living museum of Manueline architecture, Art Nouveau facades, and cobblestone streets that lead to one of the most beautiful waterfronts in Portugal.

But what earned Viana its ranking isn't the architecture — it's the people. This is a city where the fishmonger at the market remembers your name, where the café owner brings you a pastel de nata before you order it, and where strangers offer directions before you've finished unfolding the map. The warmth here is cultural, not performative.

The natural setting amplifies everything. Viana sits where the mountains meet the river meets the ocean, creating a playground for outdoor pursuits that ranges from surfing and stand-up paddleboarding to mountain biking and hiking. The beaches north of the city — Cabedelo, Afife, Moledo — are among the most beautiful in the country, with golden sand and consistent Atlantic waves.

Every August, the Romaria de Nossa Senhora d'Agonia transforms the city into one vast celebration. It's the biggest traditional festival in Portugal, with processions, traditional costumes, fireworks over the river, and a spirit of communal joy that captures everything Viana represents.

Portugal Active properties in the region consistently achieve review scores between 9.4 and 10. When your guests love the destination as much as we do, the hospitality comes naturally.

The Guardian's recognition of Armada's House as a standout destination for travellers seeking authenticity over tourism is a testament to the Portugal Active approach: properties with genuine character, in locations that reward the curious traveller.

articles.title: Video: Portugal Active Stand Up Paddle Experience
articles.content:
When our guests are asked to describe the SUP Sun Experience in a single word, the answer is always the same: magic.

The Stand Up Paddle experience takes participants along the Lima River, beginning at the medieval town of Ponte de Lima — one of the oldest towns in Portugal — and concluding at the beaches of Cabedelo where the river meets the Atlantic. Along the way, paddlers witness either a remarkable sunrise or sunset from the centre of the river, surrounded by the green hillsides and historic bridges that define this valley.

SUP can be adapted to paddlers of all levels, from complete beginners to experienced riders. Our guides know the river intimately and adjust the pace, route, and stops based on conditions and the group's experience. It's one of the most peaceful and visually stunning experiences we offer.

articles.title: Video: Portugal Active Private Yoga Session
articles.content:
Work on your strength, flexibility, and balance with our private Yoga and Pilates sessions. Whether you're a complete beginner, a seasoned practitioner, or anywhere in between, our classes are customised to your level and preferences.

Held in the gardens of our properties or on the beach at sunrise, these sessions are the ultimate way to start or end your day. Our certified instructors bring the equipment and create a practice tailored to you — no crowded studio, no fixed schedule, just movement and breath in one of the most beautiful settings in Portugal.

It's one of the most requested experiences by our guests, and once you've done yoga overlooking the Atlantic, it's hard to go back to the gym.

articles.content:

The publication featured the range of outdoor activities available through Portugal Active, from stand-up paddle tours along Cabedelo beach to bike routes through the coastal areas and natural trails.

The article noted that Portugal Active's experiences, starting from just €35, include a professional guide, all necessary equipment, and refreshments — making adventure accessible to anyone visiting the region.

The early recognition from a major health and fitness publication validated the vision behind Portugal Active: that the Minho's natural landscape is one of Europe's best-kept secrets for active, outdoor-focused holidays.

articles.title: Video: Portugal Active Sailing Experience
articles.content:
Enjoy a sailing trip with your best company along the Lima River mouth and the seaside coast of Viana do Castelo. Present your family with a different and unique experience, marked by strong emotions and views that only the water can provide.

On a sailboat, nothing is ordinary. The perspective shifts entirely when you're on the water — the coastline reveals hidden coves, the Santa Luzia basilica glows in the afternoon light, and the rhythm of the waves sets a pace that's impossible to find on land.

Our sailing experiences are suitable for all ages and experience levels. Whether you want to learn the basics of handling a sailboat or simply relax on deck while our skipper navigates the coast, the experience adapts to you.

articles.content:
Thanks to our sponsorship by GoPro, we challenged our guests to become YouTubers for a day. The Cantaert family were the first to take up the challenge, documenting their Fat Bike Wild Experience through the Minho landscape.

Fat bikes — mountain bikes with oversized tyres designed for sand and rough terrain — are one of Portugal Active's most popular adventures. The routes take riders through forest trails, along wild beaches, and across terrain that regular bikes can't handle. It's mountain biking without limits.

The resulting video captures the joy of discovery: a family exploring a new landscape together, pushing their comfort zones, and returning with GoPro footage and memories that perfectly represent the Portugal Active spirit.

articles.content:
A multi-generational family holiday at Portugal Active Lodge, told in the guests' own words. From the ultimate seafood feast to endless lunch platters, from searching for Cristiano Ronaldo football shirts to queuing for local pastries, this diary captures the joy of a family discovering the Minho together.

The adventure highlight was the Tour de Viana: seven fat bikes, a cable car ride, and mountain terrain guided by BMX champion Ronaldo Ricardo. The family swam in a secret cove, devoured ice cream and Portuguese custard tarts, and successfully built a fire that became the evening's centrepiece.

As the sun set over the Lima River and the cameras came out for the obligatory family photos, the mood was one of complete contentment. This is what family holidays are supposed to feel like — unhurried, adventurous, and full of the kind of moments that become stories told at future dinner tables.

articles.title: Guest Diary: Our First Time in Portugal
articles.content:
Adrian Lomas, founder and CEO of Blueleaf, and Alexandra Tyrer, project manager at McLaren Applied Technologies, chose Viana do Castelo for their first ever trip to Portugal. What they found exceeded every expectation.

The adventure started with fat tire bikes on the beach — deflated tyres for the sand dunes, a technique that felt completely alien to these London-based professionals. Portugal Active founder Ricardo Viana, a former national downhill MTB champion, personally guided them through the experience. Stand-up paddleboarding down the Lima River towards Viana became a highlight they still talk about.

The days filled up naturally: temple exploration by bike, swimming in natural pools, horseback riding along the beach, and dinners at local restaurants where the food was as honest as the welcome. Adrian summed it up simply: this guy really cares and loves the area.

For Adrian and Alexandra, Portugal wasn't what they expected. It was better.

articles.title: Guest Diary: From Barcelona to Portugal Active
articles.content:
Three sports enthusiasts from Barcelona — Frederico, Núria, and Enric — travelled to Viana do Castelo in June 2018 for kitesurfing and mountain biking. What they found was an experience that went far beyond sport.

From the first moment, Ricardo helped with everything. The accommodation surpassed expectations: a property with a fireplace ready, refreshments waiting, and every detail considered. Dinner at Taberna Afonso delivered what Frederico called the best cod roast he'd ever tasted.

The mountain biking took them along the Lima River eco-route to Ponte de Lima — a fantastic ride beside the river between fields and trees, followed by a challenging 600-metre climb with 20% gradients to the summit. The afternoon brought kitesurfing at Cabedelo beach in perfect conditions.

The verdict was unanimous: mind-blowing scenery, maximum comfort, great support, nature, sea, beach, adventure, friends, sports, and lots of fun. Everything a sports-focused holiday should be.

articles.title: Men's Health: Portugal Active Takes Kitesurf to Higher Education
articles.content:
Men's Health magazine covered Portugal Active's initiative to introduce kitesurfing into the higher education curriculum in partnership with the Polytechnic Institute of Viana do Castelo (IPVC). This was a world first: kitesurfing had never been part of a higher education programme anywhere.

The project's mission was the culturalisation and solidification of extreme sports in Viana do Castelo and in Portugal. By bringing kitesurfing into an academic setting, Portugal Active aimed to establish the region as a recognised centre for water sports, combining practical training with the study of sports tourism, environmental science, and outdoor education.

The partnership demonstrated Portugal Active's commitment to the Minho region that goes beyond tourism — investing in the educational infrastructure that will develop the next generation of outdoor sports professionals.
